slides.title: Environment: Living & Non-Living 🌿
slides.text: The environment is everything around us! It includes living things (plants, animals, humans) and non-living things (air, water, soil, sunlight). They constantly interact and depend on each other.
slides.spoken: The environment is everything around us! It includes living things like plants and animals, and non-living things like air, water, soil, and sunlight. They constantly interact and depend on each other.

slides.title: Plants vs Animals: Similarities 🌱🐾
slides.text: Both plants and animals are living things! They share life processes: both grow, both need food and water, both respire, both reproduce, and both respond to stimuli.
slides.spoken: Both plants and animals are living things! They share life processes: both grow, both need food and water, both respire, both reproduce, and both respond to stimuli.

slides.title: Plants vs Animals: Differences 🍃🐰
slides.text: Plants are autotrophic — they make their own food by photosynthesis using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide. Animals are heterotrophic — they cannot make food and must eat plants or other animals, moving freely!
slides.spoken: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis using sunlight and chlorophyll. Animals cannot make food and must eat plants or other animals, moving around freely to find food.

slides.title: Internal Organs: Lungs, Heart, Stomach 🫁❤️
slides.text: Internal organs are hidden inside our body! Lungs take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide. The heart pumps blood to the whole body day and night. The stomach digests food using digestive juices.
slides.spoken: Internal organs are hidden inside our body! Lungs take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide. The heart pumps blood to the whole body. The stomach digests food using digestive juices.

slides.title: Physical Features: Hills, Plains, Deserts, Valleys ⛰️🏜️
slides.text: Earth has different landforms! Hills are raised lands with slopes. Plains are flat, fertile lands perfect for farming. Deserts are dry sandy regions with little rain. Valleys are low areas between hills with rivers.
slides.spoken: Earth has different landforms! Hills are raised lands with slopes. Plains are flat, fertile lands perfect for farming. Deserts are dry sandy regions with little rain. Valleys are low areas between hills with rivers.

challenges.question: What does the environment consist of?
challenges.answer: Living and non-living things that interact
options: Living and non-living things that interact
Only living plants and animals
Only non-living air, water, and soil
challenges.hint: Think about both the living creatures and the non-living air, water, and soil around us!
challenges.misconception: The environment is NOT just plants and animals! It includes both living things AND non-living things (air, water, soil, sunlight) that interact continuously.

challenges.question: Which of these is a SIMILARITY between plants and animals?
challenges.answer: Both are living things that grow and reproduce
options: Both are living things that grow and reproduce
Both can move freely from place to place
Both make their own food by photosynthesis
challenges.hint: Think about the basic characteristics of life that both share!
challenges.misconception: Plants do NOT move around or make food the same way animals do, but both ARE living things that grow, need food and water, respire, and reproduce!

challenges.question: What is a PLAIN?
challenges.answer: A large flat or gently rolling stretch of land, good for farming
options: A large flat or gently rolling stretch of land, good for farming
A dry sandy region with very little rainfall
A high raised piece of land with a peak
challenges.hint: Think of the wide flat agricultural lands of Punjab and the Ganga basin!
challenges.misconception: A plain is flat and fertile, made by river deposits, NOT a dry desert or a steep hill! Plains are ideal for farming.
